o: Hechas, pues, estas prevenciones, no quiso aguardar más tiempo a poner en efeto su pensamiento, apretándole a ello la falta que él pensaba que hacía en el mundo su tardanza, según eran los agravios que pensaba deshacer, tuertos que enderezar, sinrazones que emendar, y abusos que mejorar y deudas que satisfacer.
t: Having made these preparations, he would wait no longer to put his plan into effect, spurred on by the lack he thought his delay was causing in the world, considering the wrongs he meant to undo, the crookedness he meant to straighten, the injustices he meant to set right, the abuses he meant to reform, and the debts he meant to pay.

o: Estos pensamientos le hicieron titubear en su propósito; mas, pudiendo más su locura que otra razón alguna, propuso de hacerse armar caballero del primero que topase, a imitación de otros muchos que así lo hicieron, según él había leído en los libros que tal le tenían.
t: These thoughts made him waver in his resolve; but, his madness being able to prevail over any other reason, he proposed to have himself knighted by the first man he met, in imitation of many others who had done the same, as he had read in the books that told of such things.

o: En lo de las armas blancas, pensaba limpiarlas de manera, en teniendo lugar, que lo fuesen más que un armiño; y con esto se quietó y prosiguió su camino, sin llevar otro que aquel que su caballo quería, creyendo que en aquello consistía la fuerza de las aventuras.
t: As for his white armour, he thought of cleaning it so thoroughly, when he had the chance, that it would outshine an ermine; and with that he calmed himself and went on his way, following no road but the one his horse chose, believing that in that lay the whole strength of adventures.

o: Yendo, pues, caminando nuestro flamante aventurero, iba hablando consigo mesmo y diciendo.
t: So our dashing adventurer went along, talking to himself and saying.

o: Y era la verdad que por él caminaba.
t: And it was the truth that he was the one who walked.

o: Y añadió diciendo.
t: And he added, saying.

o: — Dichosa edad, y siglo dichoso aquel adonde saldrán a luz las famosas hazañas mías, dignas de entallarse en bronces, esculpirse en mármoles y pintarse en tablas para memoria en lo futuro.
t: Happy age, and happy century, in which my famous deeds shall come to light, worthy to be engraved on bronzes, sculpted in marble, and painted on canvas for the memory of ages to come.

o: ¡Oh tú, sabio encantador, quienquiera que seas, a quien ha de tocar el ser coronista desta peregrina historia, ruégote que no te olvides de mi buen Rocinante, compañero eterno mío en todos mis caminos y carreras!
t: Oh you, wise enchanter, whoever you are, who shall have the task of chronicling this peregrine history, I beseech you not to forget my good Rocinante, my eternal companion on all my paths and journeys!

o: Luego volvía diciendo, como si verdaderamente fuera enamorado.
t: Then he would go back to speaking, as if he were truly in love.

o: — ¡Oh princesa Dulcinea, señora deste cautivo corazón!, mucho agravio me habedes fecho en despedirme y reprocharme con el riguroso afincamiento de mandarme no parecer ante la vuestra fermosura.
t: Oh Princess Dulcinea, lady of this captive heart! You have done me a great injury in bidding me leave and reproaching me with the strict insistence on my not appearing before your beauty.

o: Plégaos, señora, de membraros deste vuestro sujeto corazón, que tantas cuitas por vuestro amor padece.
t: Be pleased, lady, to remember this heart of yours, your subject, which suffers so many cares for love of you.

o: Con éstos iba ensartando otros disparates, todos al modo de los que sus libros le habían enseñado, imitando en cuanto podía su lenguaje.
t: With these he went on stringing together other nonsense, all in the manner of what his books had taught him, imitating their style as best he could.

o: Con esto, caminaba tan despacio, y el sol entraba tan apriesa y con tanto ardor, que fuera bastante a derretirle los sesos, si algunos tuviera.
t: With this, he walked so slowly, and the sun came on so fiercely and with such heat, that it would have been enough to melt his brains, if he had any.

o: Casi todo aquel día caminó sin acontecerle cosa que de contar fuese, de lo cual se desesperaba, porque quisiera topar luego luego con quien hacer experiencia del valor de su fuerte brazo.
t: Almost the whole of that day he walked without anything happening to him worth the telling, at which he grew desperate, for he longed to encounter at once someone with whom to make trial of the strength of his strong arm.

o: Diose priesa a caminar, y llegó a ella a tiempo que anochecía.
t: He set to walking in haste, and reached her just as night was falling.

o: Fuese llegando a la venta, que a él le parecía castillo, y a poco trecho della detuvo las riendas a Rocinante, esperando que algún enano se pusiese entre las almenas a dar señal con alguna trompeta de que llegaba caballero al castillo.
t: As he was coming up to the inn, which to him seemed a castle, after a short stretch of it he reined in Rocinante, expecting some dwarf to appear among the battlements and give signal with a trumpet that a knight was arriving at the castle.

o: Pero, como vio que se tardaban y que Rocinante se daba priesa por llegar a la caballeriza, se llegó a la puerta de la venta, y vio a las dos destraídas mozas que allí estaban, que a él le parecieron dos hermosas doncellas o dos graciosas damas que delante de la puerta del castillo se estaban solazando.
t: But seeing that they were taking a long time, and that Rocinante was in a hurry to reach the stables, he went up to the door of the inn and saw the two disheveled girls who were there, who to him seemed two beautiful maidens or two graceful ladies taking their ease before the gate of the castle.

o: — No fuyan las vuestras mercedes ni teman desaguisado alguno; ca a la orden de caballería que profeso non toca ni atañe facerle a ninguno, cuanto más a tan altas doncellas como vuestras presencias demuestran.
t: — Let not your graces flee nor fear any discourtesy; for the order of chivalry that I profess neither touches nor concerns doing harm to anyone, much less to such highborn maidens as your presences show.

o: Mirábanle las mozas, y andaban con los ojos buscándole el rostro, que la mala visera le encubría; mas, como se oyeron llamar doncellas, cosa tan fuera de su profesión, no pudieron tener la risa, y fue de manera que don Quijote vino a correrse y a decirles.
t: The girls looked at him, and searched with their eyes for his face, which the bad visor hid; but since they heard themselves called maidens, a thing so far outside their station, they could not hold in their laughter, and so it was that Don Quixote drew near to speak to them.

o: — Bien parece la mesura en las fermosas, y es mucha sandez además la risa que de leve causa procede; pero no vos lo digo porque os acuitedes ni mostredes mal talante; que el mío non es de ál que de serviros.
t: — Restraint well becomes the fair, and the laughter that springs from a slight cause is great folly besides; but I say this not that you should be troubled or show bad humor, for mine is not of a sort to serve you.

o: Mas, en efeto, temiendo la máquina de tantos pertrechos, determinó de hablarle comedidamente; y así, le dijo.
t: However, fearing the array of so many weapons, he determined to speak to him courteously; and so he said.

o: — Si vuestra merced, señor caballero, busca posada, amén del lecho (porque en esta venta no hay ninguno), todo lo demás se hallará en ella en mucha abundancia.
t: — If your grace, sir knight, is seeking lodging, welcome to the bed (for in this inn there is none); everything else will be found here in great abundance.

o: Viendo don Quijote la humildad del alcaide de la fortaleza, que tal le pareció a él el ventero y la venta, respondió.
t: Seeing the humility of the keeper of the fortress, as the innkeeper and the inn seemed to him, he replied.

o: -Para mí, señor castellano, cualquiera cosa basta, porque mis arreos son las armas, mi descanso el pelear, etc.
t: — For me, sir Castilian, anything will do, for my gear is my arms, my rest is fighting, etc.

o: Pensó el huésped que el haberle llamado castellano había sido por haberle parecido de los sanos de Castilla, aunque él era andaluz, y de los de la playa de Sanlúcar, no menos ladrón que Caco, ni menos maleante que estudiantado paje; y así, le respondió.
t: The host thought that he had called him Castilian because he had seemed to him one of the healthy men of Castile, though he was an Andalusian, and one of those from the beach of Sanlúcar, no less a thief than Cacus, no less a rogue than a page-student; and so he replied.

o: — Según eso, las camas de vuestra merced serán duras peñas, y su dormir, siempre velar; y siendo así, bien se puede apear, con seguridad de hallar en esta choza ocasión y ocasiones para no dormir en todo un año, cuanto más en una noche.
t: — According to that, your grace's beds will be hard rocks, and your sleep will be keeping watch always; and being so, one may well dismount, with the certainty of finding in this hut occasion and occasions to go without sleep all year long, let alone for a single night.

o: Y, diciendo esto, fue a tener el estribo a don Quijote, el cual se apeó con mucha dificultad y trabajo, como aquel que en todo aquel día no se había desayunado.
t: And saying this, he went to hold the stirrup for Don Quixote, who dismounted with great difficulty and effort, like one who had not breakfasted all that day.

o: Dijo luego al huésped que le tuviese mucho cuidado de su caballo, porque era la mejor pieza que comía pan en el mundo.
t: He then told the host to take great care of his horse, because it was the best piece that ate bread in the world.

o: -Nunca fuera caballero de damas tan bien servido como fuera don Quijote cuando de su aldea vino: doncellas curaban dél; princesas, del su rocino.
t: — Never was a knight of ladies so well served as Don Quixote was when he came from his village: maidens cared for him; princesses, for his nag.

o: Las mozas, que no estaban hechas a oír semejantes retóricas, no respondían palabra; sólo le preguntaron si quería comer alguna cosa.
t: The girls, who were not used to hearing such rhetoric, made no reply; they only asked him whether he wanted to eat something.

o: — Cualquiera yantaría yo —respondió don Quijote—, porque, a lo que entiendo, me haría mucho al caso.
t: — Anything would go down well with me —answered Don Quixote—, because, as I understand, it would do me a world of good.

o: A dicha, acertó a ser viernes aquel día, y no había en toda la venta sino unas raciones de un pescado que en Castilla llaman abadejo, y en Andalucía bacallao, y en otras partes curadillo, y en otras truchuela.
t: It happened that that day was a Friday, and there was in the whole inn nothing but some portions of a fish which in Castile they call abadejo, and in Andalusia cod, and in other places curadillo, and in others truchuela.

o: Preguntáronle si por ventura comería su merced truchuela, que no había otro pescado que dalle a comer.
t: They asked him whether by chance his grace would eat truchuela, since there was no other fish to give him to eat.

o: — Como haya muchas truchuelas —respondió don Quijote—, podrán servir de una trucha, porque eso se me da que me den ocho reales en sencillos que en una pieza de a ocho.
t: "— If there are lots of little trout," replied Don Quixote, "they can serve as a trout, because I am good at getting eight reales in small change rather than in a single eight-real piece."

o: Cuanto más, que podría ser que fuesen estas truchuelas como la ternera, que es mejor que la vaca, y el cabrito que el cabrón.
t: Moreover, it might be that these little trout are like veal, which is better than beef, and the kid better than the billy goat.

o: Pero, sea lo que fuere, venga luego, que el trabajo y peso de las armas no se puede llevar sin el gobierno de las tripas.
t: But, be that as it may, let it come at once, for the work and weight of arms cannot be done without the guidance of the guts.

o: Mas, al darle de beber, no fue posible, ni lo fuera si el ventero no horadara una caña, y puesto el un cabo en la boca, por el otro le iba echando el vino; y todo esto lo recebía en paciencia, a trueco de no romper las cintas de la celada.
t: But when it came to giving him drink, it was not possible, nor would it have been had the innkeeper not bored a hole in a reed; and with one end placed in his mouth, he poured the wine in through the other; and all this he endured patiently, in exchange for not breaking the straps of his helmet.

o: Mas lo que más le fatigaba era el no verse armado caballero, por parecerle que no se podría poner legítimamente en aventura alguna sin recebir la orden de caballería.
t: But what tired him most was not seeing himself armed as a knight, for it seemed to him that he could not legitimately enter into any adventure without receiving the order of knighthood.
